transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Northstar Head of Product), Ravi Patel (ML Eng), Sofia Gomez (Security), Marta Alvarez (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate y'all making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our SE. Can you all hear us ok?
[00:04] Alex: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks for doing this.
[00:08] Priya: Great, today we'll walk through our hosted API for chat and text generation, focus on streaming, common params, and how retries/backoff work. We'll also show a quick look at the Console and Optimize suggestions.
[00:15] Marta: Sounds good, main things for us: latency, cost per token, and security controls.
[00:23] Jordan: Perfect, we'll keep those front of mind. Quick question on your current stack? Ravi, you mentioned you're running models in-house?
[00:30] Ravi: Yeah, small infra team, we use a mix of internal microservices and a couple of in-house LLM endpoints on EKS. Latency's okay but cost is high and ops overhead is heavy.
[00:39] Priya: Thanks, that matches a lot of teams we talk to. For hosted API we expose simple endpoints for chat and text gen, with streaming responses over HTTP/2 or websockets. We'll demo streaming first.
[00:50] [share screen - quick Postman/terminal demo]
[00:55] Priya: So here's a basic chat request. Notice we send messages array, model param, and we can opt-in to stream=true. With streaming you get partial tokens back as they're generated, which reduces perceived latency for users.
[01:10] Alex: How are partial tokens formatted? Do we get JSON chunks or plain text?
[01:14] Priya: We stream newline-delimited JSON events, each chunk has delta text and token metadata. Example: event: message_chunk, data: {"delta":"Hello","token_index":1}. Sometimes transcription shows it as just raw text but it's JSON lines.
[01:28] Ravi: Any size limit on streaming payloads?
[01:31] Priya: Individual events are small; overall we stream until the model stops or max_tokens is reached. For mobile clients we recommend chunking on client side for display.
[01:40] Jordan: Important note: streaming doesn't change billing — tokens billed are the same as non-streaming. It's about UX not cost savings.
[01:47] Sofia: On security, does streaming expose any additional attack surface over TLS?
[01:50] Priya: No, streaming is over TLS; same auth and audit logs apply. We capture events in our audit trail and you can configure retention in Console.
[02:00] Alex: Ok great. Walk through params — temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences?
[02:06] Priya: Sure. Temperature controls randomness (0-2), default 0.7. Top_p is nucleus sampling — we recommend tuning one at a time. Max_tokens caps generation length. Stop sequences let you stop when a delimiter appears — useful for structured outputs. We also have presence/ frequency penalties for repetition.
[02:30] Ravi: We're worried about hallucinations; how do you recommend setting params?
[02:34] Priya: Lower temperature (0-0.3) reduces hallucinations; use system prompts + retrieval to ground answers. Also Optimize can recommend quantization/model choices and evals to detect regressions.
[02:46] Jordan: We'll send an example prompt set and a recommended config for your use case.
[02:51] [screen: Console - Model config page]
[02:54] Priya: In Console you can save named configs (temp/top_p/max_tokens) per route. Also routing policies — you can route by latency tier or cost tier, fallback to a cheaper model if a high-tier model is unavailable.
[03:15] Marta: Do you support pinned model versions? We can't have automatic upgrades for production endpoints.
[03:19] Priya: Yes, you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts. Rollouts are in Console with traffic split and automatic fallback rules.
[03:28] Alex: Retries — what's the recommended behavior? We have transient 5xxs on our side and want idempotent retries.
[03:35] Priya: Great question. For chat/text generation, requests are not strictly idempotent because generations differ. We recommend client-side retry on network errors with exponential backoff and jitter, but avoid automatic retries on 2xx partial responses. For safety, include an idempotency_key meta if you want server-side dedupe for certain route types (especially embeddings/batch calls).
[03:56] Ravi: How about long-running streams — if connection drops mid-stream, can we resume?
[04:00] Priya: Currently we don't support resumable streams. We recommend retry logic that will re-run the request; for deterministic output you can seed with conversation history or fix a response cache key after you receive full response.
[04:10] Alex: Any rate limits we should be aware of?
[04:14] Jordan: Hosted API has tiered rate limits; we'll include your expected qps in the pricing doc and can adjust for trial. We also support token-based quotas and per-route throttling.
[04:25] Sofia: Encryption at rest and key management — we use Azure Key Vault and need to know if Redwood can integrate with our KMS.
[04:33] Priya: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we provide server-side encryption and we have KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. We'll attach KMS integration notes to the security package.
[04:45] [05:00] Priya: Back to streaming: small note, front-end should handle partial chunk order and dedupe if you retry; sometimes transcription will mislabel names like Redwood Infer instead of Redwood Inference — that's just speech-to-text.
[05:15] Alex: Haha noted. Demo time — show a sample with temperature changes.
[05:19] [05:20] Priya: Running a prompt with temp 0.0 (deterministic) ... response comes back concise. Now temp 0.9 ... you see it's more creative and longer. We can also set stop sequence '\n###\n' to end when the model emits that token.
[06:05] Ravi: For production, we need consistent latency under 200ms p50 for short responses. Can you achieve that with hosted?
[06:12] Jordan: For short prompts and streaming start, many customers see sub-200ms starts for small models. p90/p95 depends on model and region. Dedicated capacity gives better p95 SLOs. We can run a benchmark with your prompts to validate.
[06:28] Alex: Cost question — how do conversation history tokens count?
[06:32] Priya: All input and output tokens cost; we recommend summarization to trim long histories or use KV caching for common prefixes. Optimize suggests batching and prefix caching to reduce unit cost.
[06:45] Sofia: Audit logs — can we export them to our SIEM?
[06:48] Priya: Yes, Console supports log export to S3/Cloud Storage and can stream audit events to a customer-managed endpoint. We'll include specifics in the security doc.
[06:58] [07:10] Jordan: Quick interlude — competitors. Alex, you mentioned looking at OpenAI and Anthropic?
[07:14] Alex: Yeah we ran a POC with OpenAI earlier, Anthropic for safety experiments. We're comparing latency and cost.
[07:21] Jordan: Reasonable. We typically show per-token unit economics and latency graphs — we'll share a benchmark template.
[07:28] Priya: Now, retries & idempotency patterns for batch inference: for embeddings and batched text gen, include an idempotency key so server can avoid double work on retries. For streaming chat it's trickier.
[07:41] Marta: Can we throttle or shape traffic from Console?
[07:44] Priya: Yes, per-route throttles, per-api-key quotas, and burst controls.
[07:49] Alex: Let's talk about Optimize — you mentioned model and quantization recommendations.
[07:53] Priya: Optimize analyzes token distributions and latency to recommend model variants (quantized vs fp16) and batching configs. It can suggest a smaller quantized model for high-throughput low-latency paths.
[08:06] Ravi: Are quantized models functionally identical? We saw odd behavior with aggressive quantization before.
[08:11] Priya: There's a tradeoff — more aggressive quantization can affect output quality. Optimize gives expected quality-impact metrics and run an eval suite to compare. We can run that on your prompt set.
[08:24] Alex: For the trial, we'd like hosted but with a plan to move to Dedicated if latency/cost require.
[08:30] Jordan: Common path. We'll include Dedicated pricing and migration steps.
[08:34] Sofia: One final security: SSO and RBAC integration?
[08:37] Priya: Yes, SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning, fine-grained RBAC in Console. We'll include a diagram for admin flows.
[08:47] [09:00] Jordan: Ok recap and next steps. We'll send pricing, security docs, and schedule the perf run. Anything else?
[09:07] Alex: If you can include a sample quickstart for Node and Go that's ideal.
[09:11] Jordan: Will do.
[09:13] Ravi: One more technical Q — do you support streaming over plain WebSocket vs SSE?
[09:17] Priya: We support HTTP/2 server-sent events and websockets for web clients; SDKs abstract that away. We'll link the SDK samples.
[09:26] [09:30] Marta: Great, thanks.
[09:32] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Thursday with the docs and benchmark scheduling.
[09:37] [Call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: some names and product terms mis-transcribed, minor filler words and crosstalk present.

End of transcript.
